### Mega menu
Site navigation whose top items open wide panels of grouped links, on native popovers.

Component ID: `mega-menu`

#### Contract

A `nav.mega-menu` holds links and `<button>`s. Each button names a `.mega-menu-panel` with `popovertarget`, so the panel is a native popover: the browser opens it, closes it on Escape or an outside click, puts it next in the Tab order and exposes the button's expanded state. There is no JavaScript and no menu role; these are links read and tabbed in order. The panel opens below the bar, spans the window less `--md-comp-mega-menu-margin`, and lays its `<section>` groups out in as many columns as fit. A `<small>` in a link is a description line. Use a menubar for application commands.

#### Syntax

```html
<nav class="mega-menu" aria-label="Main">
  <a href="/" aria-current="page">Home</a>
  <button type="button" popovertarget="products">Products</button>
  <div id="products" class="mega-menu-panel" popover>
    <section>
      <h2>Build</h2>
      <ul>
        <li><a href="/editor">Editor<small>Write and preview</small></a></li>
        <li><a href="/api">API</a></li>
      </ul>
    </section>
  </div>
  <a href="/pricing">Pricing</a>
</nav>
```

#### Rules

- `mega-menu-is-a-named-nav`: Write .mega-menu as a <nav> with an aria-label. It is site navigation: a landmark people jump to, not a generic row.
- `mega-menu-panel-is-a-popover`: Give .mega-menu-panel the popover attribute and open it with popovertarget on its button. The browser then owns opening, Escape, light dismiss and the button's expanded state.
- `mega-menu-is-not-a-composite-widget`: A mega menu is links and disclosure buttons reached with Tab. A menu, menubar or any other composite role promises arrow-key navigation it does not have; use a menubar for application commands.
- `mega-menu-items-are-not-menuitems`: Leave the bar's links, buttons and panels without menu or menuitem roles. They are reached with Tab, and those roles promise arrow keys and typeahead the mega menu does not have.

#### Guide checks

- Label every <nav> landmark with aria-label or aria-labelledby.
